title: weather.locations.coordinates

```python
weather.locations.coordinates(locations)
```

Extract ``(latitude, longitude)`` pairs in order.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                                                                                       | Description            | Default    |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|------------|
| locations | [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[WeatherLocation](`spotforecast2_safe.weather.locations.WeatherLocation`)\] | The locations to read. | _required_ |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                             |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[float](`float`), [float](`float`)\]\] | List[Tuple[float, float]]: One ``(lat, lon)`` pair per location, in the |
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[float](`float`), [float](`float`)\]\] | same order.                                                             |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#36dad814 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from spotforecast2_safe.weather.locations import (
    coordinates,
    default_german_locations,
)

print(coordinates(default_german_locations())[:2])
```
